dicas.texto: Boa observação! Se cada pacote tem 5 pedaços, que número representa 'um pacote inteiro'? E se alguém dá 6 pedaços, isso é mais ou menos que um pacote?
Você está no caminho certo! Pense: o total de pedaços dados é o numerador, e o número de pedaços por pacote é o denominador. Escreva isso como fração.
Quase lá! A fração tem 6 em cima. Qual número vai embaixo se cada pacote tem 5 pedaços?
Você está muito perto! Se cada pacote = 5 pedaços, então 6 pedaços = 6 sobre __? Complete com o número certo!
Ótima ideia converter! Quando o numerador é maior que o denominador, quantos grupos inteiros cabem? O que sobra?
Continue assim! Divida 6 por 5: quantas vezes o 5 cabe em 6? Esse é o número inteiro. O resto vira o novo numerador, com o mesmo denominador.
Muito bem! 5 cabe uma vez em 6, sobrando 1. Então o número misto tem parte inteira 1 e fração 1/5. Confira os campos m1, m2 e m3!
Você quase terminou! m1 = 1 (inteiro), m2 = 1 (resto), m3 = 5 (mesmo denominador). Preencha esses valores!
Pense: se cada unidade está dividida em 5 partes iguais, onde fica a sexta parte contando desde zero?
Conte as marcas: 0, 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5, 5/5 (=1), 6/5. A sexta marca após o zero é a posição certa!
Exato! Depois do 1 (que é 5/5), a próxima marca é 6/5. Ela está logo à direita do 1, na primeira divisão do segundo intervalo.
Você está quase lá! Na reta, o ponto deve estar na primeira marca depois do 1. Clique nessa posição!

exercicio.statement:
Brandon had packs of gum that he shared with his friend. Each pack had five pieces. He gave Luke six pieces. Describe the number of packs of gum Brandon gave away and show the value on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you.

steps.instruction: Enter the number of pieces Brandon gave in the top fraction box.
Enter the number of pieces in one complete pack in the bottom fraction box.
Represent the packs Brandon gave as an improper fraction using the two fraction fields.
Press Convert to rewrite the improper fraction as a mixed number.
Complete the mixed-number fields for the equivalent of 6/5.
Mark the value of 6/5 on the number line from 0 to 2.
Press Done after the fraction and number-line point are complete.

nodes.description: Inicio do exercicio
Exercicio completo
Enter the number of pieces Brandon gave in the top fraction box.
nodes.instruction: Enter the number of pieces Brandon gave in the top fraction box.

hints.message: Focus on the quantity Brandon gave to Luke, not on the size of one complete pack.
For this fraction, place the number of pieces given in the top box.
Look in the sentence for the number that tells how many pieces Brandon gave Luke.
Type the given-piece count into the numerator field at the top of the fraction.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca o que é parte (peças dadas) pelo que é todo (peças por pacote)
misconceptions.feedback: The number 5 describes the pieces in one complete pack. The numerator must represent the pieces Brandon gave.

nodes.description: Enter the number of pieces in one complete pack in the bottom fraction box.
nodes.instruction: Enter the number of pieces in one complete pack in the bottom fraction box.

hints.message: The denominator names the whole unit used for comparison.
For a packs-of-gum fraction, place the number of pieces in one complete pack in the bottom box.
Find the sentence that tells how many pieces each pack contains.
Type the pieces-per-pack count into the denominator field at the bottom of the fraction.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca o que é parte (peças dadas) pelo que é todo (peças por pacote)
misconceptions.feedback: The number 6 is the quantity given away. The denominator must show how many pieces are in one complete pack.

nodes.description: Represent the packs Brandon gave as an improper fraction using the two fraction fields.
nodes.instruction: Represent the packs Brandon gave as an improper fraction using the two fraction fields.

hints.message: A fraction compares the amount given with the amount that makes one whole pack.
Write the pieces given above the pieces in one pack.
Because the amount given is greater than one complete pack, the numerator should be greater than the denominator.
Use the given-piece count as the top number and the pieces-per-pack count as the bottom number.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca o que é parte (peças dadas) pelo que é todo (peças por pacote)
misconceptions.feedback: The fraction is reversed. The pieces given belong in the numerator, while the pieces in one complete pack belong in the denominator.

misconceptions.description: Aluno trata a quantidade absoluta como resposta final, sem formar fração
misconceptions.feedback: The number of pieces alone does not compare the amount with one pack. A fraction needs both the given-piece count and the pieces-per-pack count.

nodes.description: Press Convert to rewrite the improper fraction as a mixed number.
nodes.instruction: Press Convert to rewrite the improper fraction as a mixed number.

hints.message: An improper fraction can show one or more whole units plus a remaining fraction.
Use the button that opens the fields for the whole part and the remaining fractional part.
The numerator is greater than the denominator, so the conversion tool is appropriate here.
Click the button labeled ... to display the mixed-number fields.

misconceptions.description: Aluno não reconhece que 6/5 > 1 e acha que não pode ser convertida
misconceptions.feedback: This fraction is greater than one, so it can be rewritten as a mixed number. Use Convert to reveal the fields for that form.

nodes.description: Complete the mixed-number fields for the equivalent of 6/5.
nodes.instruction: Complete the mixed-number fields for the equivalent of 6/5.

hints.message: Separate the complete pack from the pieces that remain after making that pack.
Divide the numerator by the denominator; the quotient is the whole number and the remainder stays over the original denominator.
Ask how many groups of five fit into the numerator and how many pieces are left afterward.
Enter the number of complete packs in m1, the leftover-piece count in m2, and keep the pack size as m3.

misconceptions.description: Aluno ignora a unidade de referência e assume que cada peça = 1 pacote
misconceptions.feedback: The whole-number part counts complete packs, not individual pieces. Use the pack size to determine how many complete packs were made.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde quociente e resto na conversão para número misto
misconceptions.feedback: The quotient is the whole part and the remainder is the fractional numerator. Keep the original denominator for the remaining fraction.

misconceptions.description: Aluno não reconhece que 6/5 > 1 e acha que não pode ser convertida
misconceptions.feedback: The fraction is greater than one, so it has a whole part and a remaining fraction. Complete the mixed-number fields.

nodes.description: Mark the value of 6/5 on the number line from 0 to 2.
nodes.instruction: Mark the value of 6/5 on the number line from 0 to 2.

The number hint is off in this problem!

hints.message: Since the fraction represents more than one complete pack, its point must lie to the right of 1.
Use the five equal parts in each unit and locate the point one fifth beyond the first whole.
Start at 1 and move one of the five equal intervals toward 2.
Place the point at the first fifth after 1; the number-line value is ....

misconceptions.description: Aluno, acreditando que a fração é 6, marca o limite máximo da reta por falta de espaço | Aluno não entende que a unidade da reta corresponde a um pacote (5 peças) | Aluno não entende que a unidade da reta corresponde a um pacote (5 peças)
misconceptions.feedback: The value is greater than 1 but less than 2. Six pieces make one complete pack and only one additional fifth, so the point is not at 2. (Ou, se foi por outro motivo: On this number line, 1 represents one complete pack, not one individual piece. Six pieces are only slightly more than one pack.) (Ou, se foi por outro motivo: On this number line, 1 represents one complete pack, not one individual piece. Six pieces are only slightly more than one pack.)

misconceptions.description: Aluno conta as linhas/marcas (incluindo o zero) em vez dos espaços entre elas
misconceptions.feedback: Count the intervals, not the marks. One fifth after 1 is the target; moving two fifths after 1 places the point too far to the right.

misconceptions.description: Aluno usa fração de referência (1/2) quando incerto
misconceptions.feedback: One half is less than one whole, but six fifths is greater than one. The point must be to the right of 1.

nodes.description: Press Done after the fraction and number-line point are complete.
nodes.instruction: Press Done after the fraction and number-line point are complete.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that your fraction describes pieces compared with one complete pack.
Review the fraction fields, the mixed-number fields, and the point on the number line.
Make sure the point is between 1 and 2 and that it is one fifth after 1.
When every field and the number-line point are correct, select the ... button to submit.
